newsitem.title: CHILE: Telefonica, SBC said in Chile talks.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica, SBC said in Chile talks.

text.p: U.S. firm SBC Communications Inc and Spanish carrier Telefonica de Espana SA are in talks to merge their Chilean companies to give them an edge in the highly competitive local market, said El Mercurio Friday.
Telefonica owns some 43 percent of Chile's largest telecom Compania de Telecomunicaciones de Chile, while SBC and the local Luksic group control the much smaller carrier VTR SA.
The talks are at an early stage and include all areas of business, except cable television, said the paper, quoting VTR general manager Jorge Salvatierra.

"We are exploring this option, but with serious interest from both parties as we have seen growing common interests in all areas of telecommunications, leaving cable TV to one side," said Salvatierra. The companies operate Chile's largest cable TV channels and a merger of these firms would run into anti-monopolies problems.
VTR and CTC merged their mobile telephone operations last year, in a first step to the possible much larger merger.
Any deal between the two companies would shake up Chile's telecom market, which is one of the most sophisticated and competitive in the world.
Carriers have seen profits squeezed in the last two years following the deregulation of the long-distance market, where eight telecoms now battle for customers' calls.
